Key Activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information, to identify the most appropriate sources of data, and to modify existing techniques, methods and approaches or develop new ones to meet specific needs.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand the content and direction of existing programs and elaborate new program options.

Determines program priorities and milestones, and allocates and manages the human and financial resources of the program. Many program activities are conducted concurrently and occur within tight deadlines and involve a multi-disciplinary team approach where consensus must be maintained. Problems to be resolved can impact on other statistical programs and operations within the department.
Determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of statistical programs and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develop new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical operations and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of operational programs. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academia). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of operations.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and resolves analytical and operational problems. Data can come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data into a common conceptual framework, and to identify and measure relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical operations.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.
